extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, patent illustrators, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: US federal regulation specifying required content, format, and technical standards for drawings and photographs submitted in utility, design, and plant patent applications before the USPTO, including allowable media, sheet size/margins, views, labeling, and reproduction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable categories for drawings (black ink or color)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two acceptable categories for presenting drawings in utility and design patent applications: (1) Black ink: Black and white drawings are normally required. India ink, or its equivalent that secures solid black lines, must be used for drawings; or (2) Color: Color drawings are permitted in design applications and in utility applications only on rare occasions when color is the only practical medium for disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings in design applications require submission of the required number of sets and a specification reference. Color drawings in utility applications require a petition explaining necessity, payment of the fee in § 1.17(h), one set of color drawings if filed electronically (three sets if not), and a specification amendment inserting notice that the file contains at least one color drawing and that copies with color drawings will be provided by the Office upon request and fee. Color drawings must be of sufficient quality so details are reproducible in black and white. Color drawings are not permitted in international (PCT) applications (see PCT Rule 11.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — black and white
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photocopies of photographs, are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications, but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable examples include electrophoresis gels, blots (immunological, western, Southern, northern), autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological tissue sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, TLC plates, crystalline structures, and ornamental effects in design patents. If the subject can be illustrated by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Photographs must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in the printed patent. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size (§1.84(f)) and margin (§1.84(g)) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — color photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Color photographs will be accepted in utility and design patent applications if the conditions for accepting color drawings and black and white photographs have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the requirements for color drawings (petition, sets, specification language) and for black and white photographs (only practicable medium, sufficient quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided on drawing sheets and, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor's name, and application number or docket number (if no application number assigned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, this information must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be identified as 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d). Marked-up copies of amended figures with annotations must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms in drawings (formulae, tables, waveforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure (use brackets when necessary). Each group of waveforms must be presented as a single figure using a common vertical axis with time on the horizontal axis. Each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable. All sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds. Only one side of the sheet may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sheet must be reasonably free from erasures and must be free from alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size (§1.84(f)) and margin (§1.84(g)) requirements. See paragraph (b) for other photograph requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size. One of the shorter sides is regarded as the top. Acceptable sizes are: 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All sheets must conform to these sizes and be consistent across the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight but should have scan target points (cross-hairs) printed on two catercorner margin corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required margins: top at least 2.5 cm (1 inch); left at least 2.5 cm (1 inch); right at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch); bottom at least 1.0 cm (3/8 inch). These margins leave a sight no greater than 17.0 cm by 26.2 cm on A4 or 17.6 cm by 24.4 cm on 8.5x11 sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention; views may be plan, elevation, section, or perspective, and detail views on larger scale may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All views should be grouped together and arranged on the sheet(s) without wasting space, preferably upright, clearly separated from one another, and must not be included on sheets containing specifications, claims, or abstract. Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines. Waveforms may be connected by dashed lines to show relative timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded views
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views with separated parts embraced by a bracket to show relationship/order of assembly are permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exploded view is on the same sheet as another figure, it should be placed in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial views
rubrics_metrics.description: A view of a large machine/device may be broken into partial views on a single sheet or extended over several sheets if there is no loss in understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views on separate sheets must be capable of being linked edge to edge so that no partial view contains parts of another. Include a smaller scale view showing the whole formed by the partial views and indicating positions of the parts shown. Enlarged portions must be labeled as separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of multi-sheet or multipart views
rubrics_metrics.description: Where views on two or more sheets form a single complete view, the sheets must be arranged so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing any part of any view. Very long views may be divided into parts placed one above the other on a single sheet if relationships are clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure unambiguous relationships when dividing views; maintain clarity and ability to assemble complete figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional views
rubrics_metrics.description: The plane upon which a sectional view is taken should be indicated on the view from which the section is cut by a broken line, with ends designated by Arabic or Roman numerals corresponding to the sectional view number and arrows to indicate direction of sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must indicate sectioned portions using regularly spaced oblique parallel lines sufficiently apart to be distinguishable. Hatching should not impede reference characters/lead lines; may be broken where characters are inserted. Hatching should be at a substantial angle to surrounding axes (preferably 45°). Cross sections must show all materials and parts in cross section must show proper materials by hatching. Juxtaposed different elements must be hatched with different angles. In large areas, hatching may be confined to edging. Different hatchings may have conventional meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate position
rubrics_metrics.description: A moved (alternate) position may be shown by a broken line superimposed on a suitable view if this can be done without crowding; otherwise a separate view must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines for moved positions only when not crowding; use separate views otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place one view upon another or within the outline of another. All views on the same sheet should stand in same direction and preferably be readable with the sheet upright. If views wider than sheet width are necessary, sheet may be turned on its side so top becomes right-hand side; words must appear horizontal left-to-right in upright or turned orientation except standard scientific graphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views must not be connected by projection lines or contain center lines. Applicant may suggest a single view (by figure number) for inclusion on the front page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale of a drawing must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced in size to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted because they lose meaning with reproduction in different formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction characteristics. Every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight of lines and letters must be heavy enough for adequate reproduction; applies to fine lines, shading, and cut-surface lines. Lines/strokes of different thickness may be used where thickness has different meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; used to indicate surface or shape of spherical, cylindrical, conical elements; flat parts may be lightly shaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spaced lines for shading are preferred; lines must be thin, as few as practicable, and contrast with the rest of the drawing. Heavy lines on the shade side may substitute except where they superimpose or obscure reference characters. Light should come from upper left corner at 45°. Surface delineations preferably shown by shading. Solid black shading areas are not permitted except for bar graphs or color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate; elements thus represented must be adequately identified in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known devices should be illustrated by universally recognized conventional symbols. Other symbols not universally recognized may be used subject to Office approval if not likely to be confused with existing symbols and are readily identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to Office approval, or may be required by the examiner where necessary for understanding the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, letters, and reference characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain and legible and must not be used with brackets or enclosed outlines. They must be oriented in the same direction as the view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use English alphabet for letters except where another is customary (e.g., Greek for angles). Numbers/letters must be at least 0.32 cm (1/8 inch) high, not placed to interfere with comprehension (not cross lines, not on hatched surfaces). If necessary, underline reference characters placed on a surface and leave blank space in hatching. Same part appearing in more than one view must have same reference character; same character must never designate different parts. Reference characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in drawings; characters mentioned in description must appear in drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines are lines between reference characters and the details referred to. They may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible, originating in immediate proximity of the reference character and extending to the feature indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must not cross each other. Lead lines are required for each reference character except those indicating the surface or cross section on which they are placed (such reference characters must be underlined). Lead lines must be executed in same way as lines in the drawing (see paragraph (l)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at ends of lines provided their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable uses: (1) on a lead line, a freestanding arrow to indicate the entire section toward which it points; (2) on a lead line, an arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along the direction of the arrow; (3) to show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or Mask Work Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be placed within the sight immediately below the figure representing the copyright or mask work material and be limited to letters of .32 cm to .64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must be limited to elements provided by law (e.g., '© 1983 John Doe' or '*M* John Doe'). Inclusion permitted only if authorization language in § 1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification (preferably first paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight as defined in paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers, if present, must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (not in the margin) or on the right-hand side if drawing extends close to middle. Sheet numbering must be clear and larger than reference character numbers. Show number of each sheet as two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique line: first = sheet number, second = total number of sheets, with no other marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering and, if possible, in the order they appear on the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views forming a complete view must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers must be preceded by 'FIG.' If only a single view is used, it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear. Numbers/letters identifying views must be simple, clear, not used with brackets/circles/inverted commas, and larger than reference character numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place any authorized security marking outside the usable drawing area in the top margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure corrections are made in a permanent durable manner (no ephemeral edits).

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid punching or making holes in the sheets submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to other drawing rules/types
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references to other specific drawing rules: see § 1.152 for design drawings, § 1.1026 for international design reproductions, § 1.165 for plant drawings, and § 1.173(a)(2) for reissue drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specialized sections for design, international, plant, and reissue drawing requirements where applicable.
